question: ________ are NOT considered surface water.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aquifers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aquifers** are **underground layers** of **water-bearing rock**.
 
• They are **not considered surface water** because they are **beneath the Earth's surface**.
 
• **Surface water** refers to **bodies of water above the ground**, such as oceans, lakes, and rivers.
 
• **Aquifers** are a **crucial source of groundwater** but are **distinct** from **surface water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oceans**

 
 
• **Oceans** are **large bodies of saltwater** that cover the majority of the **Earth's surface**.
 
• They are considered **surface water** because they are** located** on the **Earth's exterior**.
 
• Oceans play a critical role in regulating the **planet's climate**, **weather patterns**, and **ecosystems**.
 
 
 
• **Lakes**
 
 
• **Lakes** are** large bodies** of** water** that are **surrounded by land**.
 
• They are considered **surface water **because they exist a**bove the Earth's surface**.
 
• Lakes can vary **greatly in size**, **depth,** and **characteristics**.
 
 
 
• **Rivers**
 
 
• **Rivers** are **natural watercourses **that flow from **higher to lower** **elevations**, usually towards the sea or another body of water.
 
• They are classified as **surface water** as they flow **above the Earth's surface**.
 
• Rivers play a crucial role in the **hydrological cycle**, **transporting water**, **sediment**, and **nutrients across landscapes**.
